Class StackSubListTest

java.lang.Object
myTest.StackSubListTest
public class StackSubListTest extends Object
Summary: This Test Suite verifies the behavior of the subList view implemented within the StackAdapter. The suite is divided into sections using comments to group tests by the method being tested. The tests check bounds, structural modifications, and the correct reflection of changes between the subList and its backing parent stack, maintaining compatibility with the J2SE 1.4.2 collections framework.
  • Test Case Design: The tests have been developed following the Test Driven Development methodology. The goal is to validate the View Pattern, ensuring that operations on the subList accurately manipulate only the specified range of the underlying stack.

Conventions used in the documentation of the tests:

  • Every test starts from the same state: setUp() creates a new, empty StackAdapter (stackTest) before each test, so the Pre-Condition of every test is an empty stack and all the elements used are inserted by the test itself (as described in its Test Description).
  • The content of a stack is written from the bottom (index 0) to the top, e.g. [A, B] means that "A" was pushed first and "B" is on top. The iterators traverse the stack in the same order.

    • testSizeRegularBehavior

      public void testSizeRegularBehavior()
      Summary: Verifies that size() returns the number of elements in the range of the subList.
      • Test Case Design: Standard case: range in the middle of the stack.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A", "B", "C" and "D", creates subList(1, 3) (view [B, C]) and calls size() on it.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted and no subList exists yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged: [A, B, C, D]; the subList is [B, C].
      • Expected Results: The subList size() returns 2.

    • testIsEmptyRegularBehavior

      public void testIsEmptyRegularBehavior()
      Summary: Verifies that a subList with fromIndex equal to toIndex is empty.
      • Test Case Design: Boundary case: empty range (fromIndex == toIndex) on a non-empty stack.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Integers 1 and 2, creates subList(1, 1) and calls isEmpty() on it.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted and no subList exists yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged: [1, 2]; the subList is empty.
      • Expected Results: The subList isEmpty() returns true.

    • testIsEmptyOnPopulatedSubList

      public void testIsEmptyOnPopulatedSubList()
      Summary: Verifies that a subList that contains elements is not empty.
      • Test Case Design: Range covering the whole stack.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Integers 1 and 2, creates subList(0, 2) (view [1, 2]) and calls isEmpty() on it.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted and no subList exists yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged: [1, 2]; the subList is [1, 2].
      • Expected Results: The subList isEmpty() returns false.

    • testClearRegularBehavior

      public void testClearRegularBehavior()
      Summary: Verifies that clear() on a subList removes only the elements of its range from the parent stack.
      • Test Case Design: Structural modification through the view: elements outside the range must not be touched.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A", "B" and "C", creates subList(1, 3) (view [B, C]) and calls clear() on it; then calls the subList isEmpty() and the stack size() and peek().
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted and no subList exists yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack contains one element: [A]; the subList is empty.
      • Expected Results: The subList isEmpty() returns true, the stack size() returns 1 and peek() returns "A".

    • testGetNegativeIndexThrowsIndexOutOfBoundsException

      public void testGetNegativeIndexThrowsIndexOutOfBoundsException()
      Summary: Verifies that get(int) on a subList throws IndexOutOfBoundsException for a negative index.
      • Test Case Design: Lower bound of the valid subList index range (index < 0).
      • Test Description: Pushes the String "A", creates subList(0, 1) (view [A]) and calls get(-1) on it.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted and no subList exists yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged: [A]; the subList is [A].
      • Expected Results: A java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException is thrown.

    • testGetIndexEqualToSubListSizeThrowsIndexOutOfBoundsException

      public void testGetIndexEqualToSubListSizeThrowsIndexOutOfBoundsException()
      Summary: Verifies that get(int) on a subList throws IndexOutOfBoundsException for an index equal to the subList size.
      • Test Case Design: Upper bound of the subList range: the index is valid for the parent stack but not for the view.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A" and "B", creates subList(1, 2) (view [B], size 1) and calls get(subList.size()), i.e. get(1), on it.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted and no subList exists yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged: [A, B]; the subList is [B].
      • Expected Results: A java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException is thrown.

      Summary: Verifies that get(int) on a subList throws IndexOutOfBoundsException for an index greater than the subList size.
      • Test Case Design: Index beyond the upper bound of the view.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A" and "B", creates subList(1, 2) (view [B], size 1) and calls get(subList.size() + 1), i.e. get(2), on it.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted and no subList exists yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged: [A, B]; the subList is [B].

    • testGetRegularBehavior

      public void testGetRegularBehavior()
      Summary: Verifies that get(int) on a subList uses indices relative to the start of the view.
      • Test Case Design: Index mapping: subList index i corresponds to parent index fromIndex + i.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A", "B" and "C", creates subList(1, 3) (view [B, C]) and calls get(0) and get(1) on it.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted and no subList exists yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged: [A, B, C]; the subList is [B, C].
      • Expected Results: get(0) returns "B" and get(1) returns "C".

    • testSetRegularBehavior

      public void testSetRegularBehavior()
      Summary: Verifies that set(int, Object) on a subList replaces the element and the change is visible in the parent stack.
      • Test Case Design: Non-structural modification through the view.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A", "B" and "C", creates subList(1, 2) (view [B]), calls set(0, "D") on it and checks the returned value; then checks the subList get(0) and the stack get(1).
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted and no subList exists yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is [A, D, C]; the subList is [D].
      • Expected Results: set() returns "B"; the subList get(0) and the stack get(1) both return "D".

      Summary: Verifies that add(int, Object) on a subList throws IndexOutOfBoundsException for an index greater than the subList size.
      • Test Case Design: Upper bound of the subList insertion range (index > size()); the index would still be valid for the parent stack.

    • testAddIndexEqualToSubListSizeRegularBehavior

      public void testAddIndexEqualToSubListSizeRegularBehavior()
      Summary: Verifies that add(int, Object) with index equal to the subList size appends the element at the end of the view.
      • Test Case Design: Boundary case: the largest valid insertion index of the view, which is in the middle of the parent stack.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A", "B" and "C", creates subList(0, 2) (view [A, B]) and calls add(subList.size(), "D") on it; then checks the subList size() and get(2), and the stack size(), get(2) and get(3).
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted and no subList exists yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is [A, B, D, C]; the subList is [A, B, D].
      • Expected Results: The subList size() returns 3 and get(2) returns "D"; the stack size() returns 4, get(2) returns "D" and get(3) returns "C".

    • testAddIndexRegularBehavior

      public void testAddIndexRegularBehavior()
      Summary: Verifies that add(int, Object) on a subList shifts the following elements to the right in both the view and the parent stack.
      • Test Case Design: Insertion at the beginning of a view that starts in the middle of the parent.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A", "B" and "C", creates subList(1, 2) (view [B]) and calls add(0, "D") on it; then checks the subList size() and get(0), and the stack size(), get(1) and get(2).
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted and no subList exists yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is [A, D, B, C]; the subList is [D, B].
      • Expected Results: The subList size() returns 2 and get(0) returns "D"; the stack size() returns 4, get(1) returns "D" and get(2) returns "B".

      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted and no subList exists yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged: [A, B]; the subList is [A].

      public void testRemoveIndexRegularBehavior()
      Summary: Verifies that remove(int) on a subList removes the element from both the view and the parent stack.
      • Test Case Design: Structural modification through the view, removing its first element.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A", "B" and "C", creates subList(1, 3) (view [B, C]) and calls remove(0) on it, checking the returned value; then checks the subList size(), and the stack size() and get(1).
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted and no subList exists yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is [A, C]; the subList is [C].
      • Expected Results: remove(0) returns "B", the subList size() returns 1, the stack size() returns 2 and get(1) returns "C".

      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted and no subList exists yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged: [A, B, C]; the subList is [B, C].

      public void testIndexOfMissingElement()
      Summary: Verifies that indexOf(Object) on a subList returns -1 for an element that is in the parent stack but outside the view.
      • Test Case Design: Element present in the parent but outside the range of the view.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A", "B" and "C", creates subList(1, 3) (view [B, C]) and calls indexOf("A") on it.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted and no subList exists yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged: [A, B, C]; the subList is [B, C].

    • testLastIndexOfRegularBehavior

      public void testLastIndexOfRegularBehavior()
      Summary: Verifies that lastIndexOf(Object) on a subList returns the last occurrence inside the view and ignores elements outside it.
      • Test Case Design: Duplicates inside the view and an element present only outside the view.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A", "B", "B" and "C", creates subList(0, 3) (view [A, B, B]) and calls lastIndexOf("B") and lastIndexOf("C") on it.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted and no subList exists yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is unchanged: [A, B, B, C]; the subList is [A, B, B].
      • Expected Results: lastIndexOf("B") returns 2 and lastIndexOf("C") returns -1.
